answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks using time-locked collateral bonding. Entities stake tokens into a registry to access the transaction oasis, where bad behavior triggers slashing. An attacker incurs the verifiable opportunity cost of locked capital per identity, suppressing any sudden plume of ephemeral clones. Even a lightweight sparrow agent must deposit funds to participate. However, this mechanism favors wealthy incumbents and excludes capital-constrained agents.
